name: Breezy Weather
insteadOf: Google Weather / ad-loaded weather apps that sell your location
hook: A feature-rich, ad-free weather app with Material 3 visuals and 50+ sources — forecasts, air quality, pollen, and alerts without a tracker in sight.
bullets: Forecasts up to 16 days from 50+ sources, including fully libre providers
Hourly and daily views with detailed 24-hour charts and nowcasting
Air quality, pollen, UV, and severe weather alerts alongside the forecast
Widgets, live wallpaper, custom icon packs, and automatic dark mode
benefits: No ads, no tracking — your location never becomes someone's revenue
Pick your own provider, from national met offices to self-hosted Open-Meteo
Beautiful, glanceable charts instead of a wall of numbers
Libre-only build available for anyone who wants strictly free sources
setupSteps: Install Breezy Weather from F-Droid or the project's GitHub releases
Add your location and let it pick a default source
Choose which blocks to show: precipitation, air quality, pollen, UV
Drop a widget on your home screen and set alert preferences
details: Breezy Weather is a free and open-source weather app in the Material 3 Expressive style, carrying forward the lineage of Geometric Weather after that project went closed-source. It draws on more than 50 weather sources — national services like NWS, Met Office, and Met Éireann alongside open ones like Open-Meteo and Pirate Weather — and serves forecasts up to 16 days out with hourly granularity, next-hour precipitation, nowcasting, air quality, pollen and ephemeris data, and severe weather alerts. The presentation is the point: detailed 24-hour charts, a large selection of widgets, a live wallpaper, custom icon packs, and automatic dark mode. Two things worth knowing: F-Droid ships a libre flavor (_freenet) that excludes non-free sources like AccuWeather if you want strictly open data, and the app can opt into sharing readings with other apps such as Gadgetbridge. It is LGPL-3.0 with no ads and no analytics.
setup: App (Android) — add a location and pick a source
